evidence: M-O s.v. biomes: jungle, tropical rainforest
terms.comment: Egger’s phrase, in Morgan–Owens, who doubts whether tropicus (classically “of the turning of the sun”) should be taken for “tropical”. Classical Latin says silva and describes it: Curtius’s forests of India are silvae … in inmēnsum spatium diffūsae, shady with tall trees.

phrases.latin: In hāc silvā incantātā arborēs loquuntur.
phrases.english: In this enchanted forest the trees talk.

phrases.latin: Silvae erant prope in inmēnsum spatium diffūsae prōcērīsque et in eximiam altitūdinem ēditīs arboribus umbrōsae.
phrases.english: There were forests spread over an almost boundless space, shady with tall trees rising to a remarkable height.

phrases.latin: Quam dēnsa est haec silva! Vix caelum vidēmus.
phrases.english: How thick this jungle is! We can hardly see the sky.

phrases.latin: In hāc silvā cotīdiē pluit; ideō tam viridis est.
phrases.english: It rains every day in this forest; that’s why it’s so green.

sources: Lewis & Short: silva · Lewis & Short: incanto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 204, 318, 408.
